n3db1974dcaf1: isoUDCA, a female-enriched bile acid produced by a gut bacterial consortium favored by estrogen, promotes hepatic cholesterol handling and bile acid metabolism through SREBP2-STARD4-CYP7B1 signaling, thereby alleviating chronic liver injury.
n9eec5648cf3f: ʟ-Carnitine is a nonproteinogenic amino acid highly abundant in myocytes, and both excess ingestion of myocytes and myocyte necrosis are associated with systemic inflammation. Here, we find that the pyrin inflammasome senses extracellular ʟ-carnitine through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and this leads to IL-1β-mediated inflammation. Our findings position OCTN2 as a potential target to reduce inflammation from exogenous or endogenous sources of extracellular ʟ-carnitine.
n607a90cce48d: First-in-class selective chemical targeting of USP32 uncovers its role in endosomal ubiquitin signaling. Scherpe, Vermue et al. develop a covalent USP32 inhibitor and complementary activity-based probes that reveal known and new membrane trafficking substrates and enable direct interrogation of USP32 activity in cells.
n8dd83dcc1d12: Zhang et al. demonstrate that isobavachalcone targets the deubiquitinase OTUB1 to promote PD-L1 ubiquitination and degradation in cancer cells. This regulation enhances T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment to suppress tumor growth.
n267c40d7607c: Luan et al. reveal that SOX2 condensates promote squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) progression by regulating chromatin organization and oncogene expression. The FDA-approved drug ixazomib selectively disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner, offering an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy with high translational potential.
nd9082dfcb53f: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are emerging as important regulators of immunity in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Enriched in mucosal and hepatic tissues, MAIT cells recognize microbial-derived metabolites presented by MHC class I-related molecule MR1 and rapidly exert effector functions, including cytokine production and cytotoxicity. Across GI malignancies, including hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers, MAIT cells display context-dependent roles shaped by the tumor microenvironment, microbiome, and immune signaling pathways. While they can mediate antitumor immunity, they frequently exhibit functional exhaustion or adopt pro-tumorigenic phenotypes. Therapeutic strategies aim to enhance MAIT cell activity, reverse dysfunction, and integrate them into combinatorial immunotherapy approaches. Understanding MAIT cell biology may enable their exploitation as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in GI cancers.
n031dbfdf0a8f: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) is a DNA polymerase expressed in pre-B and pre-T cells that functions in V(D)J recombination to add random nucleotides in a template-independent (TI) mode at junctions between antigen receptor gene segments. However, cellular, biochemical, and structural studies have also revealed a significant, short-length, template-dependent (TD) mode of TdT, in which it takes instructions from a template strand across a double-strand break. Here, we propose that this can occur through an intrachain fold-back synthesis to generate the short inverted repeats at V(D)J recombination junctions observed in early human lymphoid cells and within the adult human antigen receptor repertoire. This duality is also relevant to the functional and structural flexibility observed during the DNA repair process known as nonhomologous DNA end joining (NHEJ).
n38469d75b4c9: Deciphering the generation mechanisms and regulatory roles of bacterial transcript 3' termini requires large-scale 3' terminus data. We repurpose PATHOgenex, an available RNAtag-seq dataset, leveraging RNAtag-seq-specific read patterns associated with 3' termini to generate the "Bacterminome" atlas, a rich resource of species- and condition-dependent transcript 3' termini of 32 bacterial human pathogens grown under 10-12 conditions. Analysis of sequence elements near 3' termini revealed, along with the classical intrinsic terminator, other known and newly detected signatures, highlighting the wealth of termination-associated sequence elements. Intriguingly, orthologous genes with corresponding 3' termini show different termination mechanisms in different bacteria, often matching the dominant mechanism of the respective bacterial species. Analysis of condition-dependent 3' termini revealed some conservation across species, supporting the conjecture that alternative 3' termini can play a role in gene expression regulation. Our resource, available through a user-friendly web server (https://bacterminome.huji.ac.il), provides a platform for studying transcription termination at an unprecedented scope.
n94515a31a161: In an accompanying study, we identify the RPA-ZUP1 complex as a ubiquitin chain-editing machine that promotes removal of RPA from ssDNA. Because loss of ZUP1 causes pathological RPA trapping on ssDNA, cells must preserve a functional RPA-ZUP1 pool to sustain RPA turnover. How this homeostasis is achieved is unknown. Here, we show that ZUP1 is subject to ubiquitin-dependent fate control. ZUP1 ubiquitination promotes recruitment of p97/VCP and ATXN3, defining a molecular triage pathway that protects ZUP1 from premature proteasomal degradation. Opposing this, the E3 ligases UBR5 and HUWE1 define a degradative branch that limits ZUP1 abundance, with HUWE1 restricting its accumulation on damaged chromatin. We further show that cells express a naturally occurring ZUP1 isoform resistant to efficient ubiquitination and turnover, suggesting that isoform diversity provides a protected pool of chain-editing activity. Together, these findings define a homeostatic system that preserves ZUP1 while limiting its persistence on damaged chromatin.
n3ef6dc6c8787: The in vitro induction of 8-cell-like cells (8CLCs) from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) provides a model to study the regulatory principles of totipotency and zygotic genome activation (ZGA). However, the cellular dynamics underlying 8CLC emergence remain poorly understood. Here, we generate a TPRX1-EGFP/HERVL-tdTomato dual-reporter hPSC line to resolve the stepwise acquisition of totipotent-like identity. We show that 8CLC induction follows an ordered trajectory in which TPRX1 activation precedes the emergence of TPRX1+HERVL+ cells, which most closely resemble the in vivo 8-cell embryo transcriptionally. Single-cell transcriptomics and time-resolved flow cytometry further define a continuous transition from the primed state through a TPRX1+ intermediate to the HERVL+ 8CLC state. CRISPRi and RNA-directed perturbations support functional contributions of HERVL elements and HERVL-derived RNA to this transition, while potential locus-dependent mechanisms remain unresolved. Together, these findings establish sequential TPRX1 and HERVL activation as a defining feature of human 8CLC induction.
nd6870fce4a78: Jiang et al. show that Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes the tumor immune environment to overcome PD-1 resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). Mechanistic studies and a phase 1 trial support gut microbiome modulation as a promising strategy to improve immunotherapy in this common treatment-resistant disease.
n031aa9f2addf: Stromal interaction molecules (STIMs) are endoplasmic reticulum resident calcium (Ca2+ sensors that modulate Ca2+ homeostasis. Mammals express two isoforms, STIM1 and STIM2, but whether they serve redundant or distinct roles in neurotransmission remains poorly defined. Using Ca2+ imaging and electrophysiology in hippocampal neurons lacking STIM1, STIM2, or both, we examined presynaptic and postsynaptic functions of STIMs at excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Both isoforms redundantly activated store-operated Ca2+ entry and amplified presynaptic Ca2+ influx, sustaining neurotransmitter release by expanding the readily releasable pool of synaptic vesicles and accelerating vesicle replenishment. These presynaptic roles were synapse specific: STIM1 predominantly supported excitatory synapses, whereas STIM2 was critical for the inhibitory counterparts. Postsynaptically, STIM1 and STIM2 exerted opposing effects on glutamate and GABA receptor levels, such that simultaneous loss of both isoforms rescued postsynaptic function. Together, the findings show that STIM1 and STIM2 differentially tune synaptic efficacy according to synapse type and subcellular compartment.
n803581986b41: Overconsumption of foods rich in fats, sugars, and calories is a major contributing factor to increased risk for cardiometabolic disease. Ingestive experience with these foods can begin early in children, yet there is limited understanding of the impact of early life nutrition on the development of vagal afferent neurons necessary for coordinating appetitive and satiating behaviors. To address this gap, mice reared on a chow diet (control) were compared to those reared on a high-fat diet (HFDEARLY). We demonstrate that the vagally mediated satiation response to cholecystokinin (CCK) does not mature until adolescence in chow-reared mice. However, HFDEARLY exposure triggers a precocious maturation of this response, accompanied by transcriptomic changes in the nodose ganglion. Durable changes in orosensory processing and appetitive behaviors are also evident in adult female HFDEARLY mice, which consume more lipid and calorie-dense liquid diet than controls, suggesting a lasting, sex-specific vulnerability to overconsumption of palatable, energy-dense foods.
n6e7cd97ce79c: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor C (VEGF-C), a key lymphangiogenic growth factor, has been implicated in improving responses to cancer immunotherapy. We investigated the impact of VEGF-C on the efficacy of oncolytic virotherapy with avian paramyxoviruses APMV-1 (NDV) and APMV-4. Treatment of B16F10 tumors lacking VEGF-C delays tumor growth, and complete responses (CRs) are rare. In contrast, virotherapy of VEGF-C-expressing tumors leads to CRs in most mice. Rechallenged mice remain tumor- and metastasis-free for over two years, indicating durable immunity. VEGF-C-induced lymphangiogenesis correlates with high CD8+ and CD4+ T cell densities near lymphatic vessels. Spectral flow cytometry shows changes in the composition and activation of CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells and NK cells associated with CRs, including enrichment of CD8+CD25+PD-1+ effector T cells. T cell composition changes in sentinel and contralateral lymph nodes, indicating a systemic response. These findings demonstrate that VEGF-C-driven remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment enables durable CRs to APMV virotherapy.
n67225c9eceb4: Glioblastomas initially respond to radiotherapy but invariably recur, often within high-dose radiation treatment fields. Although stromal radiation responses are incompletely understood, evidence suggests that the tumor microenvironment becomes tumor-supportive after therapy. Using a genetically engineered glioblastoma mouse model, we profiled healthy brain, primary tumors, and post-radiotherapy recurrences with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence. Across 13 non-neoplastic cell types and 10 tumor cell states, we mapped transcriptional adaptations accompanying progression from healthy brain to primary and recurrent glioblastoma. We find distinct astrocyte states linked to disease stage, including reactive, non-neoplastic astrocytes and tumor cells adopting reactive astrocyte-like phenotypes. Reactive astrocyte-like tumor cells with mesenchymal and injury-response signatures are enriched after radiotherapy and persist in recurrent tumors. Receptor-ligand interactions between reactive astrocytes and tumor cells include known and putative drivers of aggressiveness. These findings highlight convergent reactive astrocyte programs in astrocytes and tumor cells as potential mediators of glioblastoma radioresistance.
n646312281262: The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway is essential for mounting robust innate immunity, yet its chronic activation can drive detrimental inflammation. Although multiple cell-autonomous mechanisms that restrain STING signaling have been reported, whether inflammatory mediators within the tissue microenvironment regulate STING activation remains elusive. Using herpes simplex virus type 1 infection as a model of STING activation, we revealed that the COX2-PGE2-PKA axis functions as a critical negative regulator of STING-mediated antiviral innate immunity. Mechanistically, PGE2 acts through the EP4-PKA cascade to induce PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)-mediated mitophagy by phosphorylating STOML2 at Ser29. This pathway facilitates the clearance of damaged mitochondria that serve as a source of immunostimulatory cytosolic mitochondrial DNA, thereby attenuating downstream STING activation and type I interferons while promoting viral replication. Together, these findings establish mitochondrial quality control as the mechanistic link between PGE2 signaling and mtDNA-dependent STING activation and identify the COX2-PGE2-PKA pathway as a druggable therapeutic target to enhance STING-mediated innate immunity.
n9136ccfb3367: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.
nb03ad83957ab: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.
nf2ef18422680: Wang et al. generate vascularized pancreatic islet organoids (VPIOs) containing organotypic vascular networks exhibiting endothelial fenestration. Vascularization enhances β cell maturation in vitro and survival under hypoxia. Following transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs establish functional connections with the host vasculature and effectively restore normoglycemia.
n5a881812522f: Ginhoux, Mulder, Arcila-Barrera, and Amit argue that macrophage identity is best understood not as a set of discrete subsets or a binary M1/M2 axis but as combinations of modular gene programs. They propose an extensible, program-based classification of macrophage states and discuss how it reframes macrophage-directed therapy from targeting individual checkpoints toward program-level reprogramming.
nc9f8f2a7a2d7: Srivastava et al. show that de novo-designed protein binders can selectively recognize the closed state of HSP90. The binders stabilize this conformation and provide new tools to study the HSP90 chaperone cycle and suggest a potential approach to HSP90 inhibition.
nfb8e8d3df4dc: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a bioactive gas essential for several physiologically important biological processes, including metabolism, acid–base homoeostasis, and chemosensing. CO2 can directly modulate these processes by stimulating or inhibiting specific cell signalling pathways, including the nuclear factor-κB, calcium, and Wingless (Wnt) pathways. One mechanism by which CO2 interacts with proteins to modulate cell signalling is through the reversible and nonenzymatic modification of α- N-terminal and lysine ε-amino groups to form the carbamate post-translational modification (PTM). Identifying carbamate PTMs is technically challenging because these modifications are readily reversible. However, emerging techniques have now made possible their identification and functional characterisation. Here, we review recent advances in experimental and computational methods to identify CO2-mediated PTMs.
nfc2fa81c3b99: Enzyme function is multidimensional, condition-dependent, and difficult to map at scale. Enzyme proximity sequencing (EP-Seq) is a deep mutational scanning method that combines a barcoded enzyme library, yeast surface display, fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), and high-throughput DNA sequencing to measure enzyme expression and catalytic activity.
n444578e6d824: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.
n3b869d82819c: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.
n85461ea325e3: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.
ncbd026f4cd08: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.
n775232b8c8e0: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.
nd46b3bb0e829: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.
nd7cb15e418f6: Kong et al. present a comprehensive resource for benchmarking somatic variant detection across variant classes and allele fractions. Using HapMap mixtures and pangenome graphs, they establish standardized benchmarking sets for evaluating sequencing technologies and variant-calling methods.
n99aa8f82a6de: Ha et al. benchmark detection strategies for mosaic mutations with low variant allele fractions (VAFs) using short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing. By cross-validating Illumina-based calls against PacBio HiFi data using cell-line mixtures generated across five institutions, they construct stratified reference sets, define realistic detection limits, and establish best practices for genome-wide analysis of low-VAF (<2%) variants in non-cancer tissues.
nb3f3b8a0e865: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection
n3473663798ae: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.
na9d16e158b7b: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.
n7db743ffd8de: Ataxin-2 (ATXN2) is a genetic modifier of TDP-43 toxicity and a promising therapeutic target in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, the mechanisms underlying its neuroprotective effects remain poorly understood. Using global proteomic profiling in yeast and mouse TDP-43 models, we establish that pbp1/ataxin-2 (pbp1 is the yeast ataxin-2 ortholog) reduction confers neuroprotection by activating orthogonal stress-adaptive pathways in neurons and glia, rather than simply reversing TDP-43-induced damage. In neurons, ataxin-2 downregulation activates glycolysis and reductive glutamine carboxylation driven by IDH1, restoring ATP production independently of impaired mitochondria. In astrocytes, it upregulates cholesterol biosynthesis via HMGCS1, enhancing trophic support to neurons. Full neuroprotection requires both mechanisms: neuronal survival is only completely rescued when ataxin-2 is reduced in neuron-astrocyte co-cultures. Importantly, ataxin-2 downregulation protects against both TDP-43 gain- and loss-of-function toxicity, broadening its therapeutic relevance. Collectively, these findings establish ataxin-2 as a regulator of stress-adaptive metabolic resilience.
n5752702ab2c5: Seagrasses are coastal foundation species that support ecosystem stability but face increasing global change. Here, we assemble a chromosome-level reference genome for the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica to investigate adaptive evolution and climate resilience. Comparative genomic analyses reveal features underlying intertidal adaptation, including ion transport, circadian regulation, and stress responses. We identify positively selected genes associated with the transition to marine environments. Population genomic analyses identify strong divergence between northern and southern populations, reflecting deep historical separation, largely independent evolutionary trajectories, and local adaptation. Selection signals are enriched in stress response and ion transport genes, among which TIP3-1 confers tolerance to both salinity and heat. Genomic offset projections indicate greater climate vulnerability in northern populations, whereas southern populations show higher adaptive potential and may serve as genetic sources for assisted gene flow. Together, our study provides a genomic framework for understanding adaptation and guiding conservation under climate change.
ne16bf5a21433: DNA supercoiling is an intrinsic consequence of transcription that must be resolved to maintain proper gene expression. How supercoiling shapes transcription dynamics in animal genomes remains unclear. Here, we acutely depleted topoisomerases in Caenorhabditis elegans and applied nascent transcription profiling, nuclear RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), histone modification mapping, and long-read sequencing to capture the transcriptional and chromatin responses to topological stress. We find that topoisomerase depletion preferentially inhibits and uncouples expression of convergent genes, while transcription initiation and coordinated expression of divergent genes are comparatively maintained. Topoisomerase degradation hinders transcription elongation globally, resulting in reduced production of longer transcripts and overall shortening of poly(A) tails. These elongation defects are not accompanied by global changes in elongation-associated histone modifications but coincide with modest reductions in promoter and enhancer marks. Our results indicate that genome architecture shapes transcriptional responses to DNA supercoiling, uncovering a topological basis for coordinated gene expression in a multicellular organism.
n4bbb5303cda2: Polycomb domains form at silenced genes and are marked by histone H3 lysine 27 tri-methylation, but it is unclear how this methylation is maintained following DNA replication in proliferating cells. Here, we use CUT&Tag chromatin profiling to track the dynamics of H3K27 methylation in human cells. We find that tri-methylation in Polycomb domains is maintained by stepwise methylation after DNA replication. Outside of Polycomb domains, thousands of transcriptionally inactive genes gain histone H3K27 di-methylation hours after DNA replication. Acute treatment with small-molecule inhibitors of the Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) histone methyltransferase slows H3K27 methylation during S-phase of the cell cycle and increases acetylation of the residue. This effect is most pronounced at Polycomb domains replicating in early S-phase, thereby suggesting that early replication and slow histone methylation confer plasticity to developmentally silenced genes. Together, our results explain how H3K27 modification patterns are faithfully duplicated in rapidly proliferating cells.
n6481dd614a2e: Encephalomyocarditis virus (EMCV) is the most widespread zoonotic pathogen that causes piglet death. EMCV enters cells via caveolin-mediated endocytosis. However, the receptors required for EMCV entry into the cells are unknown. Here, we show that intercellular cell adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) serves as a significant functional receptor during adsorption and entry. ICAM-1 binds directly to the EMCV viral proteins VP1 and VP2 with high affinity. Consistently, a soluble ICAM-1 fusion protein or anti-ICAM-1 blocking antibody impairs EMCV infection in susceptible human and mouse cells. Domain 1 of ICAM-1 is involved in the recognition of EMCV. ICAM-4 serves as a receptor in ICAM-1 knockout/knockdown mice and cell lines during EMCV infection. These findings suggest that ICAM-1 and ICAM-4 are entry receptors for EMCV and that targeting ICAM-1 D1 could be a potential strategy for the development of antivirals against EMCV.
n5f87ff682510: Gastric cancer (GC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with a strong propensity for lymph node metastasis. To characterize the metastatic ecosystem, we perform integrated single-cell transcriptomic and T cell receptor profiling of 156,871 cells from 30 primary tumors and matched sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs), spanning non-metastatic and metastatic tumors and SLNs from non-metastatic to micro- and macro-metastatic states. We identify LN-enriched progenitor exhausted T cells as a potential reservoir for tumor-infiltrating exhausted CD8+ T cells and reveal dynamic remodeling of the lymph node microenvironment by tumor-associated macrophages during disease progression. We further show that ILC3s promote a pro-metastatic microenvironment in micro-metastatic lymph nodes through the AREG-EGFR axis, facilitating lymphatic dissemination and subsequent establishment of CD24+ tumor cells. Collectively, these findings provide a stage-resolved view of the tumor-lymph node metastatic ecosystem and identify potential therapeutic targets in GC.
nda903f244e23: Alphaherpesviruses, including herpes simplex viruses (HSV-1/2) and pseudorabies virus (PRV), pose significant threats to human and animal health, yet broad-spectrum interventions remain elusive. Here, we characterize C12A6, a neutralizing antibody (nAb) targeting glycoprotein B (gB) that cross-neutralizes HSV-1, HSV-2, and PRV and confers substantial, although incomplete, therapeutic protection against lethal HSV-1 or PRV infection. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of C12A6 in complex with PRV gB and HSV-2 gB reveal that the antibody engages a conserved conformational epitope on Domain I (DI). A conserved interaction framework, anchored by invariant polar contacts and a hydrophobic core, supports recognition across divergent alphaherpesvirus gBs. Comparison with the broader alphaherpesvirus antibody 16F9 shows that C12A6 additionally engages less-conserved peripheral residues, providing a structural basis for its more restricted recognition breadth. These findings define the structural basis for C12A6-mediated cross-neutralization and illuminate the functional architecture of gB DI as a target for broad-spectrum antiviral development.
n92c3da9c552d: Neuronal activity induces topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B) to form DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within the promoters of early response genes (ERGs), such as Fos and Npas4, and facilitates rapid ERG transcription. However, the mechanisms that repair activity-induced DSBs and their significance for neuronal function remain ill-defined. Here, we report that depletion of tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase 2 (TDP2) in cultured mouse cortical neurons delays the repair of TOP2B-mediated DSBs and prolongs ERG expression following neuronal stimulation. Deleting Tdp2 in excitatory forebrain neurons in vivo caused DSB accrual, ERG overexpression, and increased excitatory synaptic transmission and cortical circuit dysfunction. Whereas proliferating cells utilize alternative pathways to process TOP2B-mediated DSBs, we find that such mechanisms are relatively inactive in postmitotic neurons. Overall, these results indicate that TDP2-mediated DNA repair is crucial for the temporal control of ERG transcription and suggest that defective repair of activity-induced DSBs could underlie neurological abnormalities in individuals with TDP2 mutations.
n731756dee9f6: Although a loss-of-function variant of TM6SF2 is a highly penetrant risk factor for steatotic liver disease, including progression to cirrhosis and cancer, its normal function is largely unknown. Here we show that endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized TM6SF2 forms membrane contact sites (MCSs) with late endosomes/lysosomes, where it activates the small GTPase RAB7 to enable an endolysosomal route for selective secretion of lipid-rich very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) particles. In accord, TM6SF2 and RAB7 deficiency similarly cause endolysosomal VLDL retention and accumulation of enlarged late endosomes/lysosomes. TM6SF2 further binds to VAMP-associated protein (VAP) ER-anchor proteins to maintain MCSs between the ER, endosomes, and the trans-Golgi network, with TM6SF2 deficiency causing Golgi fragmentation and disruption of cGAS-STING signaling known to prevent cirrhosis and cancer by clearing senescent hepatocytes. Our findings establish TM6SF2 as an ER-MCS component that enables endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintains Golgi structure, which suggests that TM6SF2 loss of function causes liver disease through steatosis-dependent and independent mechanisms.
n2c6683ad4213: Predicting which patients will benefit from cancer immunotherapy remains challenging. Braun et al. use live tumor tissue from routine needle and forceps biopsies to measure ex vivo immunotherapy response. Results are consistent with clinical outcomes in a small patient cohort, including patients misclassified by current biomarker tests.
na92fadf8eee5: Wang et al. demonstrate that high-current transcranial temporal interference stimulation targeting sgACC alleviates depression safely and delivers stronger short-term therapeutic effects than low-current or sham stimulation.
nd6bebe49f738: Akay et al. use a genome-wide CRISPR screen to identify Wnt signaling as a regulator of lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes. Stimulating Wnt signaling by inhibiting GSK3B reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in iPSC-derived brain organoids and APOE4;PS19 mice.
nee552d79d25c: Guo et al. develop a multiplex lineage-tracing platform to systematically profile fibroblasts across all five anatomical layers of the skin. They uncover a highly coordinated, multi-stage sequence of fibroblast mobilization and architectural reorganization during wound healing, demonstrating that cell-intrinsic programs predominate over local microenvironments to govern layer-specific contributions.
n302cf0a48a7a: Daniel L. Kastner, physician-scientist, geneticist, mentor, and scientific leader, transformed our understanding of human inflammatory disease. His death is a profound loss not only to the immunology community but also to the numerous patients and families whose illnesses he elucidated—and for whom, in many cases, he developed effective treatments. Called the “father of autoinflammatory diseases,” Dan did more than discover individual disorders: he defined an entirely new category of human disease.
n028466f3b40e: Metabolic reprogramming regulates immune cell function; however, how metabolic signals instruct early monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Yang et al. show that LDHA-dependent cytosolic NAD+ regeneration promotes selective HIF1α translation, supporting commitment to a protective NOS2+ macrophage fate and revealing a broader link between redox metabolism and cell fate decisions.
n856af4ff701e: Qin et al. demonstrate that extrachromosomal DNA hubs function as inherent electrochemical reactors. By non-enzymatically generating a localized antioxidant shield, these hubs protect themselves from oxidative damage. Disrupting this spatial redox balance triggers ecDNA degradation, exposing a distinct vulnerability in ecDNA-positive cancers.
nc1cdbc532110: Müller, Kolesnikova, Doudin, et al. reveal a structural mechanism for residue-specific nucleosome acetylation by capturing the MSL histone acetyltransferase during catalysis. Their findings provide a foundation for understanding how H4K16 acetylation links transcription to changes in chromatin structure, a mechanism essential for Drosophila dosage compensation and implicated in human disease.
ndda0bb09677c: Lyu et al. show that the interaction between the deubiquitinase OTULIN and the ubiquitin ligase LUBAC restrains LUBAC autoubiquitination and activity. Disrupting this interaction enhances Met1-linked ubiquitination at the TNF receptor complex, which increases NF-κB signaling and sensitizes mice to TNF-dependent toxicity. Thus, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction restricts Met1-linked ubiquitin signaling.
nc4620e7122b1: A weakness in glycobiology research is the insufficient integration of approaches used to connect glycan structure to function. From glycogene knockouts to understanding glycan structures, dynamics, and interactions, to determining whether a single glycan structure underlies a specific cellular function, no single approach provides sufficient information to establish these relationships. We argue that resolving glycan structure–function relationships requires the integration of complementary approaches spanning genetics, analytical glycomics, glycoengineering, structural biology, and computational modelling. The field stands at a transition point: from cataloguing glycan structures to understanding their diverse roles in regulating the biology of health and disease. Such an integrated approach will be critical for translating structural glycan information into mechanistic insights and, ultimately, informed glycoengineering and therapeutic design.
n249258f20d07: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.
n28047ded39fc: Phenotype measurement scale has long been known to impact genetic inference, yet it is often ignored in modern studies. Costantino et al. characterize how the choice of phenotype scale affects the results of common analyses. They find that it can change GWAS hits and PGS × E interactions and influence PGS performance in specific subgroups.
nc741b8d7d370: The brain must balance the automatic extraction of regularities with top-down cognitive control, yet the hemispheric contributions of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) remain unresolved. Here, we applied inhibitory repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation to the left, right, or bilateral DLPFC in 95 adults during a probabilistic sequence learning task. We found that inhibiting the right and bilateral DLPFC enhanced statistical learning compared to sham stimulation. Contrary to the hypothesis that interference from existing knowledge would mediate this effect, episodic memory performance was unaffected. As an alternative, we propose that right DLPFC inhibition shifts cognitive processing toward an exploratory information-sampling strategy, supported by our finding of greater reaction time variability in the right and bilateral stimulation groups. Our results provide causal evidence for a right-lateralized suppressive influence of the DLPFC on unsupervised learning and suggest that its role is linked to information-processing style rather than direct competition with episodic memory systems.
nb6dc2a4cb4ff: Fatty acids require conjugation with coenzyme A (CoA) for their incorporation into membrane lipids. Of these, very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs), the precursors of yeast ceramides, are particularly hydrophobic. Yet, it remains unresolved where and how the sole VLCFA-CoA synthetase Fat1 activates them. Here, we show that lipid droplets (LDs) are both the site of free VLCFA storage and their place of activation. Free VLCFAs preferentially partition into LDs in molecular simulations and in vitro reconstitutions, whereas Fat1 targets the LD surface in cells via an N-terminal amphipathic helix. Structural predictions identify an essential hydrophobic cavity in Fat1 that connects the active site to the membrane, suggesting that VLCFAs shuttle directly from the LD core into the enzymatic pocket. Our model explains how the organelle targeting of a fatty acid activator evolved to match the biophysical properties, and consequently, the subcellular localization of its highly hydrophobic substrate.
nf2fd166a9f48: The mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt), which promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and proteostasis, is regulated by the transcription factor ATFS-1. In C. elegans, impaired atfs-1 expression perturbs mitochondrial function and slows development. Here, using an RNAi suppressor screen, we find that inhibition of the nuclear hormone receptor NHR-180 increases mitochondrial function and developmental rate in atfs-1(null) worms. NHR-180 levels increase and become more nuclear-localized during mitochondrial dysfunction, inducing transcription of genes required for protein synthesis on cytosolic and mitochondrial ribosomes. The NHR-180 ligand-binding domain interacts with AMP, suggesting that NHR-180 may link cellular energy status to protein synthesis during mitochondrial stress. However, NHR-180-dependent activity is associated with exacerbated mitochondrial dysfunction. Consistent with these findings, inhibition of the S6 kinase homolog RSKS-1 increases mitochondrial function in atfs-1(null) worms. S6 kinase inhibition also increases respiration and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) content in mammalian ATF5-knockout cells and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS)-deficient models.
n62cfd8a1b241: Transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) drive genomic instability and are linked to tumorigenesis and treatment response. Replication stress exacerbates TRCs, but how cells coordinate transcription and replication to limit these conflicts remains unclear. Here, we identify NONO as a key regulator that maintains transcription-replication balance via BRD4 under replication stress. Replication stress triggers NONO acetylation at K243, enhancing BRD4 binding. On single-stranded DNA, NONO-BRD4 form condensates that block paused RNA polymerase II (RNAP2) release, fine-tuning elongation. NONO loss causes aberrant accumulation of elongating RNAP2 at termination regions, promoting TRCs and genomic instability. Conditions that increase origin firing, including ATR inhibition or BRCA2 deficiency, further exacerbate this phenotype in NONO-deficient cells, leading to pronounced synthetic lethality. Together, these findings define a NONO-mediated surveillance mechanism that couples replication stress to transcriptional restraint via condensate-dependent regulation of BRD4, and identify NONO as a potential therapeutic target in replication stress-driven cancers.
n34d687d6c026: Early-life adversity (ELA) is strongly linked to emotional disorders characterized by dysregulated reward behaviors. However, the mechanisms by which transient neonatal experiences generate enduring, sex-specific alterations in brain function remain unresolved. Paraventricular thalamus (PVT) neurons are selectively activated during ELA and contribute to disrupted adult reward behaviors. Here, we explore the molecular mechanisms behind these enduring, sex-specific disruptions. Combining activity-dependent genetic labeling with translating ribosome affinity purification, we find distinct gene translation programs in ELA and control mice of both sexes. Notably, the receptor for the neuropeptide corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor type 1 (Crhr1), is differentially expressed across rearing and sex in response to reward. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated Crhr1 deletion exclusively in early-life-activated PVT neurons normalizes reward behaviors in both male and female adult ELA mice. Thus, CRHR1 signaling in adult PVT neurons activated by ELA is a required and potentially targetable mechanism underlying sex-specific, ELA-induced disruptions of reward behaviors.
n120bba3fc1a9: RNA polymerase III (Pol III) transcription produces RNAs involved in core biological processes and is therefore coupled to fluctuating demands for protein synthesis and cell growth. However, the mechanisms underlying dynamic Pol III regulation remain incompletely understood. To address this gap, we investigated protein-protein interactions shared across multiple Pol III subunits to characterize the macromolecular interactome of Pol III, with special attention directed toward potential regulatory factors. Our survey uncovers interactions between Pol III and the NuRD (nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase) complex. We further show that NuRD localizes to active Pol III-transcribed genes, including tRNA gene clusters associated with notably high expression. Inhibiting NuRD-associated deacetylase activity increases Pol III transcription at these sites, suggesting that NuRD constrains Pol III activity and thereby modulates the dynamic range of Pol III-derived RNAs. These findings implicate NuRD as a chromatin-based mechanism linking signaling events and metabolic need with the dynamic availability of specific tRNA pools.
n4b53e510b405: Gao et al. identify protein kinase (PKR) as a non-canonical stimulator of interferon genes (STING) effector in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury. STING oligomerization at the endoplasmic reticulum drives PKR-S33 autophosphorylation and TBK1-independent IKK-NF-κB activation. This pathway induces LAMP3-dependent lysosomal cell death, and its inhibition attenuates epithelial injury.
nd7eab5a7939f: Why does performance pressure sometimes cause choking but sometimes elicit exceptional performance? We propose that pressure shifts the complexity of information-processing rules that guide action. Performance improves when shifts move processing toward task-matched complexity and deteriorates when they promote maladaptive simplification, overcomplexification, or the use of rules that exceed available processing resources.
nd3b305961c8f: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.
n2a01732cc6c8: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.
nf0f8318ec4c4: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.
n352689535a20: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.
nd9d7d6cec6b0: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.
n7262ca68982b: Daily light-dark cycles impose environmental fluctuations that require coordinated regulation of physiology. This coordination is mediated by the circadian clock, which operates as a network of tissue oscillators; however, the signals that convey circadian information between organs remain incompletely defined. We identify nicotinic acid riboside (NaR) as a circulating metabolite whose rhythmicity depends on the liver clock. In adipocytes and neuronal cells, NaR engages the unfolded protein response (UPR). Proteome-wide stability profiling implicates the prefoldin complex as a target of NaR, linking NaR exposure to altered proteostasis. In adipocytes, NaR-induced UPR signaling converges on the transcription factor CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein alpha (CEBPA). Sustained NaR exposure suppresses adipocyte lipid deposition, whereas temporally restricted NaR stimulation enhances adipogenesis. Together, these findings identify NaR as a liver clock-controlled circulating metabolite that couples systemic circadian metabolism to proteostasis and tissue remodeling, revealing a mechanism by which temporal metabolic signals shape tissue-specific physiological outcomes.
ndac6434c35a9: Context modulates sensory processing. Recent proposals claim early areas like primary visual cortex (V1) are only influenced by "local" context (e.g., recent stimulus history), while "global" context (e.g., learned patterns and probabilities) modulates only higher areas. We tested this using a global/local oddball paradigm: mice viewed repeating five-item sequences (AAAA-B), where B is deviant from local context but typical in global context. Using two-photon imaging and local field potential (LFP) recording in mouse V1, we found that global predictability normalized responses to B stimuli. This effect emerged after fewer than 10 sequence repetitions, demonstrating rapid learning. When a globally deviant "C" stimulus replaced B or when B occurred at unpredictable intervals (i.e., standard oddball), V1 showed strong response enhancement. This global context modulation in V1 required top-down feedback from anterior cingulate area. However, when B was replaced by an A (AAAA-A), responses were mixed, suggesting that stimulus-specific adaptation can constrain prediction-error signals in V1.
n2e740822d71b: Patients with neuropathic pain frequently present with emotional disorders. Cellular plasticity within anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is considered as a key interface linking pain and emotion. However, mounting efforts have been devoted to elucidating intracellular mechanisms of plasticity, how extracellular alterations trigger intracellular changes remains elusive. Thrombospondin (THBS), a key component of extracellular matrix (ECM), is involved in various pathophysiological processes. Here, we show that THBS4 is downregulated in the ACC following peripheral neuropathy. Overexpressing cingulate THBS4 alleviates pain hypersensitivity and anxiodepression. Mechanistic analysis indicates that THBS4 maintains glutamate homeostasis via direct regulation of excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2) in astrocytic membrane, further stabilizing abnormal plasticity of pyramidal neurons and eventually producing analgesic, anxiolytic, and antidepressive effects. Taken together, we show THBS4-mediated neuron-astrocyte crosstalk as a key mechanism underlying neuropathic pain and comorbid anxiodepression. Recombinant THBS4 protein represents a promising therapeutic strategy for treatment of neuropathic pain and anxiodepression.
nae7eed3235e5: High endothelial venules (HEVs) are specialized post-capillary venules that gate lymphocyte entry into lymph nodes, yet human in vitro models that capture their specialization remain limited. Here, we develop a perfusable human HEV-on-chip in which blood endothelial cells (BECs) form an engineered microvessel within a collagen-fibrin matrix populated by human fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs). The presence of FRCs, without exogenous LIGHT, drives HEV-associated marker expression (PNAd/MECA-79 and VCAM-1) and a plump endothelial wall enwrapped by a thickened laminin+ basement membrane, recapitulating features of lymph-node HEVs. Functionally, HEV-like vessels support markedly increased T-lymphocyte adhesion while preserving VE-cadherin junctions. Introducing MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells in an adjacent channel reduces MECA-79, disrupts junctional organization, and increases permeability without inducing apoptosis. Together, this platform defines a stromal instruction program for human HEV identity and a tractable model of cancer-associated HEV dysfunction.
n7b6e7a8d9e74: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) drive pro-tumorigenic signaling but also promote lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, making ROS regulation critical during high oxidative stress stages of tumor progression, such as metastasis. Loss of the antioxidant TIGAR in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells raises ROS and enhances metastatic behavior but also sensitizes cells to ferroptosis. To understand how TIGAR-null cells survive to metastasize, we examine the role of macrophage infiltration, which is increased in TIGAR-null tumors. Co-culturing TIGAR-null PDAC cells with macrophages protects them from ferroptosis. The tumor cells induce macrophage IL-6 secretion, which leads to the activation of STAT3 and upregulation of the iron-sequestering protein ferritin (FTH1) in cancer cells. FTH1 depletion in TIGAR-null cells restores ferroptosis sensitivity and reduces lung metastasis. These results suggest that the outcome of increased ROS in tumors may depend on the activation of mechanisms that selectively prevent ferroptosis while preserving ROS-induced oncogenic signaling and metastasis-promoting pathways.
n725ebb91ed90: Transcriptional interference is the in cis suppression of one transcriptional process by another. To define the mechanisms by which transcriptional readthrough is converted into stable gene silencing, we develop a mouse cell line model of cobalamin C deficiency associated with MMACHC silencing (epi-cblC) by deleting the Prdx1 intron 5 splice acceptor, thereby inducing antisense transcription across Mmachc. Readthrough results in ectopic H3K36me3 deposition, de novo DNA methylation, and stable silencing of Mmachc. Through systematic perturbations of transcription and the H3K36 and DNA methylation machinery, we demonstrate that antisense transcription is the primary driver of repression, whereas H3K36me3 contributes directly to promoter silencing and is further required for the establishment of DNA methylation, which in turn confers long-term stability. Together, these findings define a hierarchical silencing cascade by which transcriptional readthrough establishes stable gene repression and demonstrate that transcription itself can direct local chromatin remodeling and changes in gene expression.
n5de238110afc: High-risk neuroblastoma remains a leading cause of pediatric cancer mortality, underscoring the need for novel therapeutics. MYCN amplification drives transcriptional addiction, creating vulnerabilities for therapeutic intervention. Inhibition of CDK12, a key regulator of transcription elongation, downregulates DNA damage response (DDR) genes. CDK12 inactivation using protein degraders and small molecules, including the orally bioavailable, selective CDK12/13 inhibitor OKI-1546, induced BRCAness and apoptosis in neuroblastoma cells. High-throughput compound screening combined with CDK12 inhibition/degradation revealed synergistic interactions encompassing multiple biological pathways. Merestinib, a multi-kinase inhibitor, emerged as the top synergistic agent across a panel of neuroblastoma in vitro models. Combining OKI-1546 with merestinib amplified DDR downregulation and diminished MYCN-driven signaling. OKI-1546 treatment reduced tumor growth and extended survival in vivo, which was enhanced when combined with merestinib. Whilst further in vivo validation is warranted, our findings nominate CDK12 as a promising therapeutic target in high-risk neuroblastoma, which can be exploited through combinatorial treatments.
nf4908790bb33: Coordinated locomotion depends not only on motor programs but also on the sensory feedback that refines them. Proprioceptive sensory neurons (pSNs) modulate motor circuits through direct synapses, yet their role in shaping spinal cord circuits has remained unclear. Here, we uncover an essential function for pSNs in organizing Clarke's column (CC) neurons, a major spinocerebellar population. Although CC neurons are born early in embryogenesis, their distinctive columnar architecture emerges postnatally and depends on direct pSN input. Genetic ablation of pSNs reduces the number of CC neurons and disrupts their somatic and dendritic organization. Blocking neurotransmission or eliminating Piezo2-dependent mechanotransduction produces overlapping defects, revealing that both the presence and activity of pSNs are required for CC maturation. RNA sequencing identifies a molecular signature of pSN-dependent regulation, implicating the axon guidance receptor Unc5c as a candidate regulator. Our findings reveal an unrecognized role for pSNs in spinal circuit development.
n6a660ae88841: Transcriptional regulation is mediated by enhancers, yet how genetic perturbations alter enhancer activity and gene expression remains unclear. We develop UDI-UMI-STARR-seq, integrating dual indexes and unique molecular identifiers, and combine it with RNA-seq to profile perturbation-associated changes in enhancer activity and gene expression. We apply this approach to 253,632 fragments representing 46,142 cell type-specific candidate enhancers and assess the impact of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of six transcription factors (ATF2, CTCF, FOXA1, LEF1, TCF7L2, and SCRT1). We identify responsive fragments that are repressed or induced and enriched for p53 family motifs. Enhancer-gene mapping reveals associations between responsive fragments and gene expression changes, including Wnt/p53 targets after ATF2 or LEF1 depletion. A deep learning model recapitulates enhancer grammar, including cooperative motif syntax and flanking sequence context. Applying this framework to 16p12.1 deletion identifies responsive fragments associated with genes involved in neuronal function, providing a scalable readout of enhancer dynamics across genetic perturbations.
n78ac3a1379aa: The blood-brain barrier (BBB), formed by brain endothelial cells (BECs), creates a safe and homeostatic environment for proper brain function. While BECs are extraordinarily thin, their luminal and abluminal plasma membranes face markedly different environments: the blood and brain parenchyma, respectively. How BBB membrane proteins are spatially distributed between these membranes and the factors regulating their localization are not clear. Here, we establish a method for measuring polarized protein sorting at the BBB in vivo. We characterize the distribution of transporters and receptors on the luminal and abluminal plasma membranes and identify protein-intrinsic motifs that control polarized sorting. Finally, we observe a change in membrane protein distribution that aligns with circadian rhythms, revealing an under-appreciated dimension of BBB dynamics. This method can be broadly used for evaluating membrane protein landscape changes during development and disease and for choosing optimal molecular targets for BBB-crossing therapeutics.
ndb6ff0c2583f: Various ribosome-associated quality control pathways safeguard translation fidelity by detecting and resolving aberrant translation events. Recently, a pathway that senses stalled ribosomes with an occluded A-site has been described. The small molecules NVS1.1 and ternatin-4 induce ribosome stalling by trapping eukaryotic release factor 1 (eRF1) and elongation factor 1A1 (eEF1A1), respectively, within the ribosomal A-site, thereby promoting their ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Additionally to the previously identified factors GCN1, RNF14, and RNF25, we identify here the deubiquitinase USP9X as a regulator of this pathway. In the absence of USP9X deubiquitinase activity, eRF1 is still ubiquitinated but fails to undergo efficient degradation. However, compared with wild-type cells, K6-linked ubiquitin chains accumulate on eRF1 in cells lacking USP9X activity, suggesting that USP9X trims K6-linked ubiquitin chains during a late step of substrate processing. Furthermore, clearance of trapped eRF1 engages a feedback mechanism involving 4EHP and the integrated stress response (ISR) to suppress translation, whereas impaired degradation prevents translational shutdown.
n5cc8b582a59b: Gene fusions in cancer are traditionally understood to generate hybrid proteins with altered functions that promote malignancy. Here, we define a previously unrecognized class of oncogenic fusions that preserve protein structure but replace the 5' untranslated region (5' UTR), thereby rewiring translational regulation. Using the MET oncogene as a paradigm, we show that 5' UTR-replacing fusions, identified across >200,000 cancer samples, increase MET protein abundance 5- to 10-fold without corresponding changes in mRNA levels. The resulting receptor remains correctly localized, ligand-responsive, and active, thereby promoting cell survival and motility. These fusion transcripts are detected following irradiation, documenting UTR rewiring in a post-treatment context. Beyond MET, similar 5' UTR-replacing fusions occur in FGFR1, JAK2, and NTRK2, where partner-derived 5 'UTRs are associated with reduced regulatory complexity and enhanced protein output. Together, our findings establish UTR rewiring as an overlooked mechanism of oncogene overexpression with implications for cancer genome annotation and precision oncology.
n577324ec4e19: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.
n232536a222ef: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.
n89e6ec2dfce9: Bai et al. reveal a PARP1-mediated m6A feedback mechanism involving IGF2BPs and the METTL3/METTL14 writer complex. They further show that combined targeting of ADP ribosylation and m6A leads to synergistic anti-tumor effects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.
n3cd9da96f6d5: Retrons help bacteria defend against phage by initiating a toxic response to restrict viral propagation. Here, Zhang et al. describe the non-canonical mechanism of Retron-Vpa2, which accumulates msDNA in response to phage triggers and regulates its toxic response on a translational level through a highly structured hybrid RNA.
n038f844d330f: Shin et al. present cryo-EM structures of the SPβ integrase along the integration and excision pathways that provide mechanistic insights addressing the long-standing questions of how large serine integrases enforce highly directional DNA recombination and how the cognate recombination directionality factor leads to a complete reversal of directionality.
n20f04c827951: Li et al. systematically map splicing within and between transposable elements (TEs) across cancers and define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts. TEtrans display distinct regulatory programs and can function as oncogenic RNAs or encode immunogenic tumor antigens, expanding the functional landscape of TE reactivation in cancer.
n5d58caad6e4e: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.
nbd63ddd156f9: Höppner et al. show that disease-associated substitutions in PTH1R helix-8 selectively rewire receptor coupling to G proteins and βarrestin. Distinct mutations bias PTH1R engagement toward either Gαq or βarrestin pathways and impair Gαs activation. These findings reveal mutation-driven shifts in effector selectivity as a previously unrecognized mechanism in PTH1R-associated disease.
n9b41ae99e8c8: Recursive splice sites are rare motifs postulated to facilitate splicing across massive introns and shape isoform diversity. The necessity of recursive splicing (RS) and its role in human disease are unsubstantiated. Here, we use CRISPR to model intronic deletions eliminating an RS site (RS1) in CADM2 and conferring risk for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and other neurobehavioral traits. Ablating RS1 in human induced neurons alters the gradient of RNA abundance across CADM2's first intron, decreases CADM2 expression, and impacts transcript usage. Decreased CADM2 expression is reflected in reduced exon usage downstream of RS1 and global alteration to genes involved in neuronal processes. In vivo rodent models harboring Cadm2 RS1 deletions exhibit an attenuated effect on Cadm2 expression and modest changes in behavior and functional brain connectivity. This study demonstrates RS as a noncoding regulatory mechanism in a gene associated with a spectrum of neuropsychiatric and behavioral traits.
n1e6c0ce12a96: Diffuse gastric cancer is highly metastatic and lacks effective therapeutic targets. Using membrane proteomics, gastric cancer cell models, biophysical measurements, and in vivo metastasis assays, we identify EpCAM as a regulator of membrane-cytoskeletal mechanics. EpCAM overexpression was associated with reduced apparent plasma membrane tension, ERM-actin remodeling, increased traction forces, and nuclear deformation. Functional perturbation of ezrin and lamin A/C supported the involvement of membrane-cytoskeleton-nucleus mechanical coupling in confined migration. EpCAM knockout or monoclonal antibody blockade reduced tumor invasion and lymph node dissemination in vivo. These findings establish a mechanobiological framework linking EpCAM-dependent membrane mechanics to metastatic behavior and highlight EpCAM-associated mechanical regulation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in diffuse gastric cancer.
ned2c9eed1c87: Newborns are especially susceptible to bacterial meningitis, primarily caused by group B Streptococcus (GBS), due to incomplete maturation of immune and barrier systems. While meningitis is well known to break down the blood-brain barrier, its effect on the meningeal arachnoid barrier remains poorly understood. Using a neonatal bacterial meningitis model, we demonstrate that GBS infection significantly increases arachnoid barrier permeability, disrupts tight junctions, and elevates meningeal production of proinflammatory cytokines. CD206+/LYVE-1+ border-associated macrophages undergo morphological and molecular activation post-infection, but their depletion prior to infection does not attenuate arachnoid barrier leakage or cytokine levels. We show that meningeal fibroblasts are a source of proinflammatory cytokines in response to GBS infection and that a systemic exposure of TNF-α alone is sufficient to induce barrier breakdown. These results support that the neonatal arachnoid barrier is vulnerable to cytokine-induced breakdown and highlight the role of non-immune meningeal cells like fibroblasts during bacterial infection.
nf44318c6e385: Proper nucleosome positioning is essential for gene regulation and genomic integrity. Current models posit that chromatin regulators override histones' intrinsic sequence preferences to establish nucleosome landscapes observed in vivo, implying a minimal role for DNA sequence in guiding nucleosomal structure. In contrast, we show that DNA sequence intrinsically guides nucleosome structure and remodeling from yeast to mammals. Nucleosomes with weak translational settings in vitro, in yeast, and in mammalian cells display strong rotational positioning that favors inward-facing A/T and outward-facing G/C dinucleotides at 10 bp spacings. Foreign DNA sequences heterologously inserted into the yeast genome obey the same rules, indicating that DNA sequence itself is causal. Remodelers and transcription elongation shift the preference among translational positions 10 bp apart, which maintains the same rotational setting. We propose that DNA sequence creates an energy landscape with preferred rotational settings, and that chromatin regulators navigate within, rather than override, these preferences.
n718909ec8591: Wang et al. develop an oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for colorectal cancer immunotherapy, which triggers ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells to boost immunogenicity, while the bacterial adjuvanticity reshapes the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This approach activates both systemic and gut mucosal immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic tumor growth and metastasis.
nf3a2a5dfdcc8: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are heterogeneous, but how pathogenic subsets drive relapse in allergic dermatitis remains unclear. Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ CD4+ TRM subset sustained through CXCL16-dependent clustering with CD301b+ cDC2s, revealing the TRM-DC niche as a potential therapeutic target for allergic dermatitis.
n6bc218949b2c: How metabolic enzyme levels are regulated is poorly understood. Studying the tryptophan (Trp)-metabolizing enzyme TDO2, Thielen et al. discover a CK2 kinase-β-TrCP E3 ligase pathway that regulates stability in response to substrate availability. Trp occupation of an exosite restricts degron accessibility, whereas low Trp releases the degron for phosphorylation-ubiquitylation-mediated degradation.
n695f93081a8a: Liang et al. identify phytanoyl-CoA dioxygenase domain containing 1 (PHYHD1) as a tumor suppressor that regulates protein production in kidney cancer. Loss of PHYHD1 promotes disease progression by increasing ceramide transporter 1 (CERT1) production, uncovering a regulatory pathway that may help predict patient outcomes and provide a therapeutic opportunity for PHYHD1-deficient tumors.
nf720614dfc33: Bonsor et al. determined the crystal structure of the KRAS-BRAF(RBD-CRD) complex, revealing reduced KRAS engagement by BRAF(CRD) compared with CRAF(CRD). They further show that the BRAF-specific region (BSR) attenuates RBD binding to KRAS, while inclusion of the CRD partially relieves this inhibition.
nf50730d9c221: Predictions of cysteine reactivity rely heavily on acidity (pKa) data from dilute solutions. However, the intracellular milieu is crowded and dynamic, with substrates, cofactors, and metabolites that modulate reactivity, thereby affecting cell signaling and metabolic adaptation. This forum argues that Cys pKa values are necessary but insufficient, proposing an integrated, microenvironment-dependent framework.
n155a01f71f65: Despite growing evidence that dopamine acts as an innate immune inflammatory mediator, the molecular mechanisms by which dopamine modulates human immune function are incompletely defined. Here, we define the pathway in which dopamine induces robust IL-6 secretion in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages (hMDMs) through mitochondrial stress. Dopamine initiates a transient mitochondrial membrane depolarization that leads to sustained alterations in mitochondrial dynamics, including morphology and metabolism. These events promote the release of mtDNA into the cytoplasm, triggering the cGAS-STING pathway and NF-κB signaling. Pharmacological inhibition at multiple nodes of this pathway attenuates IL-6 secretion, establishing mitochondrial dysfunction and cGAS-STING signaling as central mediators of dopamine-driven IL-6 secretion. Variability in dopamine receptor expression across donors correlates with the magnitude of IL-6 responses. These findings highlight a potential link between dopamine signaling and systemic inflammation and suggest that differences in dopamine receptor expression may contribute to inter-individual variation in innate immune responses.
n44587ea54ba4: The middle and lower Yellow River regions were crucial for early agricultural development and the emergence of complex societies in East Asia, yet their fine-scale population history from the Neolithic to historical periods remains incompletely resolved. Here, we present genome-wide data from 61 ancient individuals (∼4,500-200 before present [BP]) from Henan and Shandong. Our analyses show that middle-to-late Neolithic populations at Dahecun in Henan are genetically homogeneous and closely related to contemporaneous Yellow River millet-farming populations. By ∼3,000 BP, Shandong populations shift toward a late Neolithic middle Yellow River-related ancestry profile, consistent with the eastward expansion of middle Yellow River agricultural populations. This ancestry profile persists into historical periods, indicating long-term genetic continuity in Shandong. Two Tang-Song-period individuals from western Shandong carry ∼15% West Eurasian-related ancestry, indicating limited cross-regional genetic interaction. These findings refine the population history of the middle and lower Yellow River regions.
nbbc426d037f7: HIV persistence in CD4+ T cells and brain microglia is maintained by host mechanisms that enforce viral latency. We identify ENL and the deubiquitinase USP7 as a host complex that sustains HIV latency. Pharmacologic inhibition or genetic loss of ENL reactivated latent HIV. Proteomic analyses revealed an ENL-USP7-BRD4 regulatory axis associated with latency maintenance, where USP7 maintained BRD4 protein stability. Targeted USP7 degradation using PROTAC induced latency reversal and destabilized BRD4. Chromatin immunoprecipitation studies showed that ENL was required for USP7 and BRD4 occupancy at the HIV nuc-1 region but not at the 5' long terminal repeat. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing further implicated this pathway in HIV persistence within the central nervous system. Importantly, degradation of either ENL or USP7 reactivated latent HIV in resting CD4+ T cells and brain microglia from individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy. These findings identify the ENL-USP7-BRD4 axis as a therapeutically actionable mechanism sustaining HIV latency and viral reservoirs.
nc7255fb8e658: RNA fingerprinting is a statistical framework that infers causal regulators from single-cell experiments by mapping their transcriptional responses onto reference perturbation dictionaries.
n339bcbe92910: Chromatin reader inhibitors require robust cellular assays for target-engagement profiling. Recchia et al. develop modular Acyl-eCR reporters that enable scalable live-cell measurement of bromodomain inhibitor specificity and PROTAC activity, providing a versatile platform for chromatin-targeted drug discovery.
n076b6f73ae4b: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) modulate myeloid cells but are absent early after ischemic stroke when neutrophil infiltration peaks. Whether promoting their early infiltration into the brain as an introduced niche could modulate the cerebral immune micromilieu remains unknown. Here, we show that splenic Tregs at day 5 post-MCAO (ischemia-conditioned Tregs, ICTregs) exhibit enhanced adhesion. Transferred ICTregs infiltrate the infarcted area early, alter brain cellular composition, reduce neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and preserve blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity during the acute phase. Mechanistically, integrin α4 anchors ICTregs to cerebral venous endothelium, and ICTreg Annexin A1 interacts with neutrophil Dectin-1 to suppress NETs. The transcription factor Ikzf2 is critical for ICTreg induction, and modulating Ikzf2 enables Sham Tregs to acquire early brain-homing capacity. These findings offer valuable insights into the neuroprotective function of ICTregs in the early stage of ischemic stroke and identify engineered-Tregs target for optimizing the brain-immune ecosystem for neural protection.
n9a51659ed626: The release of bacterial bioactive molecules across the gut barrier is a crucial yet poorly understood step in host-microbe communication. Here, we identify a phage-driven mechanism associated with this process in the beneficial symbiont Lactiplantibacillus plantarum NC8 (LpNC8). We show that a stress-responsive prophage, pp2, undergoes activation and triggers holin-lysin-mediated bacterial lysis, leading to the production of infectious phage particles and increased extracellular recovery of bacterial vesicles carrying lipoteichoic acids. In a model of nutritional symbiosis, pp2-dependent lysis is required for LpNC8 to promote juvenile growth in undernourished Drosophila melanogaster. Disruption of prophage-mediated lysis impairs vesicle recovery and host growth promotion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the copper cell region of the Drosophila midgut acts as a physiological trigger of prophage induction. Together, our findings link host intestinal physiology to prophage activity and bacterial lysis, revealing phage-driven lysis as a mechanism contributing to beneficial bacterial-host interactions during nutritional stress.
nb43785e83752: DNA motif discovery and, particularly, computational modeling of transcription factor binding motifs, has been a mecca of algorithmic bioinformatics for several decades. Here, we report the results of the largest open community challenge in Inferring BInding Specificities (IBIS), where participants all over the world were invited to construct binding specificity models from multi-assay experimental data for poorly studied human transcription factors. The submissions were rigorously tested against a rich held-out dataset. Benchmarking demonstrated a consistent advantage of properly designed deep learning models over traditional positional weight matrices and other machine learning methods. Yet, the positional weight matrices displayed a surprisingly strong performance out of the box, being only slightly behind the best deep learning models. A post-challenge assessment of a selection of other deep learning methods further solidified this finding. IBIS highlights the power of benchmarking in finding adequate DNA motif representations, emphasizes the pros and cons of various machine learning methods applied to DNA motif modeling, and establishes a rich dataset, benchmarking protocols, and computational framework for a fair cross-platform evaluation of future models of transcription factor binding motifs in DNA sequences.
ne6e4c41411c8: Centromeres are essential regions of the genome that ensure chromosome segregation during mitosis but are also hotspots for chromosome breaks and rearrangements in cancer. The mechanisms underlying this fragility are not fully elucidated. Here, we show that oxidative DNA damage destabilizes centromeres and promotes chromosome instability. Using a chemoptogenetic system to generate singlet oxygen locally at centromeres, we uncouple centromeric oxidative damage from global oxidative stress. Oxidative base lesions slow DNA synthesis, destabilize CENP-A chromatin, and generate DNA breaks that persist into subsequent cell cycles. Single-cell time-lapse imaging reveals cell-cycle-dependent outcomes, with lesions before or during replication favoring quiescence and post-replicative lesions allowing mitotic progression but compromising daughter-cell proliferation. Finally, in pre-tumorigenic cells, centromeric oxidative lesions lead to mitotic defects, aneuploidy, and whole-arm chromosome translocations. Collectively, we identify centromeres as cell-cycle-sensitive DNA damage sensors and oxidative stress as a direct driver of centromere fragility and chromosome instability.
nbbc33d8c87b1: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) plays a critical role in alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). Pectin improves ALD partially through the AhR pathway. However, AhR is expressed across different organs and cell types, and the specific cellular targets mediating AhR's effects in ALD remain unclear. We generated conditional AhR knockout mice in intestinal epithelial cells, hepatocytes, dendritic cells, and Rorγt-positive cells, in which AhR may play a critical role in regulating the gut-liver axis and pectin protection against ALD. ALD was induced using the Lieber-DeCarli model, and mice received pectin supplementation. AhR deficiency in intestinal epithelial cells and hepatocytes in mice leads to increased hepatic inflammation and serum ALT following alcohol administration compared with their littermate controls. However, pectin exerted strong protective effects against ALD in all the models. Our results suggest that AhR activation across multiple cell types, rather than a single cell type, mediates the protective role of pectin.
n3623de86684d: Symmans et al. review how artificial intelligence supports RNA therapeutic development in precision oncology, spanning multi-omics target prioritization and RNA design to delivery, patient stratification, manufacturing, and clinical translation. They distinguish clinically supported applications from preclinical and speculative approaches, outlining validation, governance, and regulatory requirements.
n93ed1f40f36f: Citrano, Maheswari Jawahar et al. develop sensitive immunoassays using second-generation polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies against HDGFL2-CE proteins and show that their levels in brain tissue associate with pTDP-43 pathology, earlier symptom onset, and shorter survival in patients with FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND.
